papers.title: Dual homeostatic and circadian resonance shapes REM episode duration.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This paper extends the wave model of sleep dynamics by adding a circadian resonance to explain REM episode duration profiles. The constrained model reproduced various profiles and identified REM duration as a quantitative marker of homeostatic-circadian alignment.

papers.title: The circadian system is affected by Alzheimers disease independently from amyloid beta deposits
papers.summary: The study investigated circadian disruption in APP/PS1 mice, finding reduced REM sleep, altered body temperature rhythms, hyperactivity of melanopsin-expressing retinal ganglion cells at young age and hypoactivity at older ages, and changes in SCN connectomics and gene expression without amyloid plaques in the ventral hypothalamus. These findings suggest AD affects the circadian system independently of amyloid-beta deposits.

papers.title: A distributed-delay Wilson-Cowan model of sleep-related rhythms in the corticothalamic system
papers.summary: This study models the corticothalamic circuit with a Wilson-Cowan model including distributed delays, showing that delays can alter stability and oscillatory dynamics, producing sleep spindle and infra-slow rhythms. The temporal structure of feedback is crucial for rhythm generation.

papers.title: SEDAT: A hybrid tokenizer for large EEG models.
papers.summary: The paper introduces SEDAT, a hybrid tokenizer for EEG foundation models that combines spatial aggregation, signal decomposition, adaptive segmentation, and frequency-domain resampling. Evaluated on 10 diverse EEG datasets with four large models, SEDAT improves classification accuracy by up to 15.3% over fixed-length windowing and shows better feature separability, with lower computational complexity.

papers.title: The DYNAM-O Toolbox: Characterizing Individualized Neural Signatures in Sleep EEG
papers.summary: This paper presents the DYNAM-O Toolbox, an open-source software for analyzing sleep EEG by detecting transient oscillations as time-frequency peaks. Analysis of data from 133 adults revealed sex differences in oscillatory activity beyond conventional spindle ranges.

papers.title: Transcriptome and proteome associated to the sex-dependent effects of Neuroligin-2 absence on wakefulness and sleep features
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of Neuroligin-2 (NLGN2) absence on sleep/wake phenotypes and cortical omic profiles in male and female mice. They found sex-dependent changes in sleep architecture and electrocorticographic activity, with less than 31% of transcriptomic and 15% of proteomic changes shared between sexes, indicating that NLGN2 effects on sleep and molecular landscapes differ by biological sex.

papers.title: CaMKIIα mediates feedback effects of wheel-running activity on the circadian pacemaker in mice.
papers.summary: This study shows that CaMKIIα mediates feedback effects of wheel-running activity on the circadian pacemaker in mice, affecting entrainment patterns and period. The effects are modeled with a two-oscillator system where CaMKIIα influences coupling.

papers.title: Chronic trazodone treatment consolidates sleep, improves memory, and reduces amyloid pathology in a mouse model of Alzheimers disease
papers.summary: Chronic trazodone treatment in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease consolidates sleep, improves memory, and reduces amyloid pathology, including a 45% reduction in hippocampal plaque burden in aged mice.

papers.title: Tilia Tomentosa promotes sleep, preserving sleep structure.
papers.summary: This study investigates effects of Tilia tomentosa extract on sleep in mice, finding increased NREM sleep and reduced wakefulness during active hours without disrupting sleep structure. Spectral analysis showed mild changes in gamma and theta bands, suggesting a sleep-promoting effect.

papers.title: Looking back: tracing the origins of sleep across the animal kingdom.
papers.summary: This review discusses the evolutionary origins of sleep, proposing that sleep evolved to restrict activity to one temporal niche and that circadian processes predate neurons. It synthesizes evidence suggesting sleep is an ancient process involving conserved molecular oscillators and signaling molecules present even in species without centralized nervous systems.

papers.title: Biological and Habitual Factors That Influence Sleep and Circadian Rhythm: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes biological and habitual factors influencing sleep and circadian rhythm, including gene haplotype, chronotype, gut microbiome, and modifiable variables like meal timing and physical activity. It identifies research gaps and suggests that manipulating these factors can improve sleep and circadian alignment.

papers.title: Pathogenic tau in the mouse locus coeruleus produces noradrenergic hyperactivity and neuropsychiatric phenotypes reminiscent of early Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: The study developed a mouse model of early Alzheimer's disease with pathogenic tau expression in locus coeruleus neurons, finding that tau pathology induces noradrenergic hyperactivity, anxiety-like behaviors, compulsive behavior, and reduced sleep spindles. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed changes in neuronal excitability and synaptic/metabolic alterations, suggesting mechanisms for early neuropsychiatric symptoms.

papers.title: EEG microstate reconfiguration across cognitive states in preschool children with developmental language disorder.
papers.summary: This study examined EEG microstate organization in preschool children with developmental language disorder (DLD) versus typically developing peers across three cognitive tasks. Findings show microstate features vary by task context, but no robust DLD-specific alterations were found, suggesting limited evidence for microstate changes in this sample.

papers.title: The ups and downs of heart rate during sleep: a source of heterogeneity in individuals with obstructive sleep apnoea.
papers.summary: This study analyzed heart rate (HR) distributions during sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) versus non-SDB periods in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). It identified four chronotropic response patterns (bradycardic, tachycardic, mixed, neither), with bradycardic patients showing more severe apnea and higher hypoxic burden, highlighting heterogeneity in autonomic responses.

papers.title: In-home validation of wrist actigraphy against portable electroencephalography for sleep assessment in older adults.
papers.summary: This validation study compared wrist actigraphy against in-home portable EEG for sleep assessment in 49 community-dwelling older adults over 217 nights. Actigraphy provided acceptable estimates of average total sleep time but showed substantial errors for sleep onset latency and wake after sleep onset, indicating limited accuracy for these indices in this population.

papers.title: Rapid phase resetting of Aedes aegypti circadian rhythms by transient alterations in light exposure
papers.summary: This study systematically manipulated light schedules in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and found that a single day of altered lighting, particularly a 6-hour light pulse, induces rapid phase shifts in circadian rhythms without masking. Phase shifts were primarily driven by light-offset, highlighting the plasticity of mosquito behavior in response to artificial light.

papers.title: Integrating Spatial-Temporal Channel Reliability with AI for Robust High-Frequency Oscillation Detection in Intracranial EEG.
papers.journal: International IEEE/EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering : [proceedings]. International IEEE EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering
papers.summary: The authors developed a reliability-guided HFO detection pipeline incorporating event-level denoising, channel signal quality assessment, and segment-level temporal reliability analysis. Applied to iEEG data, the pipeline improved SOZ localization accuracy from 66% baseline to 93% after filtering, enhancing clinical specificity.

papers.title: A Double-Blind Randomised Controlled Crossover Trial of the Effect of Blue-Enriched Ambient Light on Sleep in Older Adults With Sleep Disturbance: The CleverLights Study.
papers.summary: This randomized crossover trial exposed 12 older adults with sleep disturbance to blue-enriched ambient light during the day and reduced blue light in the evening, finding no significant improvement in wake after sleep onset. However, exploratory analyses showed increased sigma EEG activity during sleep and an altered distal-proximal skin temperature gradient, suggesting potential effects on sleep physiology.

papers.title: ViSTA-SleepNet: A View-Integrated and Subject-Adaptive Transformer Framework for Multimodal Sleep Staging.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The paper introduces ViSTA-SleepNet, a two-stage multi-view multimodal transformer framework for sleep staging that integrates EEG, EOG, and EMG signals with demographic information. It achieved accuracies of 88.5%, 84.5%, and 89.6% on Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, and SHHS datasets respectively, with over 95% accuracy in spindle and slow-wave detection.

papers.title: Differences in circadian rhythm changes between myopic and non-myopic college students over 2 years.
papers.summary: This 2-year cohort study of college students found that myopic students had later bedtimes, earlier wake-up times, and lower chronotype scores at baseline. Over follow-up, only myopic students showed a 45-minute delay in dim-light melatonin onset, indicating significant circadian rhythm changes in myopia.

papers.title: Integrating socioeconomic context with multimodal EEG data for improved ADHD risk screening.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning model that combines EEG signals and socioeconomic context to screen for ADHD risk. The model outperformed EEG-only baselines in epoch-level cross-validation, achieving accuracy improvements of 2.1-5.9% and sensitivity gains up to 12.2%, but subject-independent results were more modest, suggesting it is a proof-of-concept.

papers.title: Impaired midfrontal‑motor theta phase synchronization characterizes maladaptive motivational behavior in people with obsessive‑compulsive disorder.
papers.summary: This study used a motivational Go/NoGo learning task with EEG to examine maladaptive biases in OCD. People with OCD showed stronger Pavlovian bias and lower learning rates, and while they displayed increased midfrontal theta power related to conflict detection, midfrontal-motor theta phase synchrony was not enhanced and failed to modulate these biases, revealing a neural mechanism for the insight-action dissociation.

papers.title: Preliminary field evaluation and exploratory external-association analysis of a modified wellness questionnaire for short-term monitoring in elite male water polo players.
papers.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
papers.summary: This study evaluated a modified wellness questionnaire for short-term monitoring in elite male water polo players, analyzing internal consistency, reliability, and associations with external variables over 12 occasions. The questionnaire showed acceptable internal consistency for fatigue and recovery composites, but low between-athlete reliability for most items, with sleep duration and previous-day training load associated with next-day wellness scores.

papers.title: T-2 Toxin Disrupts Alzheimer's-relevant App/Tau Homeostasis via Circadian-p53-Senescence Crosstalk: Evidence from Human Neuroblastoma Cells.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of low-dose T-2 toxin on Alzheimer's-relevant protein homeostasis in SH-SY5Y cells, revealing that T-2 toxin remodels APP and Tau via a CLOCK-p53-senescence axis. Pharmacological targeting of CLOCK and p53 or senolytic treatment attenuated these changes, suggesting intervention strategies.

papers.title: Prenatal road traffic noise impairs early testicular development in Sprague-Dawley offspring: pharmacological rescue by melatonin and edaravone; developmental preservation by environmental enrichment.
papers.summary: This study exposed pregnant rats to road traffic noise and found reduced testicular development in male offspring, including lower organ weights, testosterone, and antioxidant enzymes, plus increased oxidative stress and inflammation. Combined melatonin and edaravone treatment or environmental enrichment restored normal development, identifying RTN as a modifiable risk factor and suggesting pharmacological rescue strategies.

papers.title: The circadian architecture of tumor immunity: mechanistic insights and treatment strategies.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that the circadian clock regulates tumor immunity and that circadian disruption promotes tumor progression by reshaping the immune microenvironment. It discusses circadian-targeting interventions and chronotherapy as potential strategies to enhance cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Circadian-based individualised protection against inflammation-cancer transition in atrophic gastritis patients.
papers.summary: This review proposes a predictive, preventive, and personalized medicine framework for managing chronic atrophic gastritis based on circadian rhythms. It integrates digital biomarkers, multi-omics, and chronotherapy to address the inflammation-cancer transition, reframing circadian rhythm as a targetable axis.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-Based Measures to Understand Meditation and Mindfulness: Bibliometric Scoping Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.journal: Global advances in integrative medicine and health
papers.summary: This bibliometric scoping review mapped randomized controlled trials (RCTs) using EEG-based measures for meditation and mindfulness-based interventions, identifying 142 eligible publications from 31 countries. Significant heterogeneity was found in study populations, experimental designs, and outcomes, indicating that further systematic reviews require more original studies.

papers.title: Disparities in sleep-disordered breathing: epidemiology, mechanisms, and pathways toward equity- a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines disparities in sleep-disordered breathing, including higher prevalence, severity, and lower treatment adherence among racial and ethnic minorities and underserved populations. It highlights social determinants and proposes multilevel interventions to achieve equity.

papers.title: Sleep quality and its clinical correlates in axial spondyloarthritis: a cross‑sectional study with exploratory mediation modelling.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study of 119 axial spondyloarthritis patients found 52.9% were poor sleepers, with poor sleep quality significantly associated with higher disease activity, pain, fatigue, worse function, and quality of life. Depression and anxiety were independent predictors of poor sleep, and mediation modeling suggested they partly mediate the relationship between longer disease duration and poor sleep.

papers.title: Cyclical women's health needs at work: Low-disclosure support and privacy-preserving self-tracking in age-stratified focus groups in Japan.
papers.summary: In age-stratified focus groups with 21 Japanese working women, participants described menstrual leave as impractical due to stigma and norms, relying on informal coping. Privacy-preserving self-tracking was seen as potentially useful if workplaces provided safe channels for low-disclosure micro-accommodations, but the study notes these are perceptions of feasibility, not demonstrated effects.

papers.title: The Efficacy of Therapies for Phantom Limb Pain in Amputees Assessed via Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) and Electroencephalography (EEG) Measures of Cortical Reorganization: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: A scoping review of seven studies found nonpharmacologic therapies for phantom limb pain often associated with measurable changes in cortical organization in M1 and S1, with mirror therapy consistently reducing pain and normalizing sensorimotor activity. However, the relationship between cortical changes and pain reduction is inconsistent, suggesting PLP is a multifactorial, network-level condition.

papers.title: Markerless Motion Capture Reveals Movement Abnormalities in Isolated REM Sleep Behavior Disorder
papers.summary: Markerless motion capture from single RGB-camera videos was used to classify isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) versus healthy controls from 93 walking videos, with the best model achieving AUROC 0.739. The approach outperformed MDS-UPDRS III and identified hip-related temporal features as key contributors, suggesting potential for scalable prodromal Parkinson's disease screening.

papers.title: A multimodal sleep intervention improves sleep quality and architecture in chronic insomnia: a prospective exploratory study.
papers.summary: A prospective exploratory pilot study of 30 patients with refractory chronic insomnia found that a multimodal intervention combining stellate ganglion block, CBT-I, and anesthetic-assisted sleep induction significantly reduced PSQI scores by about 8 points at follow-ups up to 6 months. It also increased deep and REM sleep proportions without serious adverse events, but requires randomized controlled trials for confirmation.

papers.title: Association between sleep duration and risk of new-onset gastric diseases in middle-aged and older adults: A prospective cohort study in China.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study analyzed data from 7,539 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) to examine the association between sleep duration and new-onset gastric diseases. Shorter nighttime sleep duration was associated with an increased risk of new-onset gastric diseases, with each interquartile range increase in nighttime sleep reducing risk by 14%.

papers.title: Smartphone addiction and multisite musculoskeletal pain among parents: The potential mediating role of sleep disturbance and the moderating role of physical activity.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional survey study of 1,444 parents found a weak positive association between smartphone addiction and multisite musculoskeletal pain burden. Sleep disturbance partially mediated this association, and physical activity moderated it, with the association weaker at higher physical activity levels.

papers.title: Airway-derived mechanical power and postoperative pulmonary complications in obese adults undergoing laparoscopic bariatric surgery: a secondary analysis of a randomised trial.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a randomized trial in 160 obese adults undergoing laparoscopic bariatric surgery examined associations between airway-derived mechanical power and postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs). Mean total mechanical power showed an inverted U-shaped association with PPC risk, while dynamic mechanical power showed no significant association.

papers.title: Migration-driven exposome reconfiguration: a predictive, preventive and personalized medicine perspective on cardiometabolic risk.
authors: Elizabeth Aparecida Ferraz da Silva Torres
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how migration-driven exposome reconfiguration influences cardiometabolic risk in migrant populations, integrating environmental, psychosocial, and behavioral stressors. It proposes a PPPM/3PM framework using biomarkers, digital health, and multi-omics for proactive, personalized prevention.

papers.title: Academic Stress and Temporomandibular Disorder Symptoms in Dental Students: Preliminary Cross-Sectional Study Findings on Prevalence, Severity, and Associated Factors.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional multicenter survey of 756 dental students found that 56.6% had temporomandibular disorder (TMD) symptoms, and academic stress was moderate to severe in a majority. Female gender and prior TMD diagnosis were associated with TMD symptoms, but academic stress was not significantly associated after adjustment.

papers.title: Acute total sleep deprivation transiently increases plasma total tau but not plasma P-tau181 in healthy adults.
papers.summary: In this exploratory study, 20 healthy adults underwent 24h total sleep deprivation followed by recovery sleep. Plasma total tau increased by 35% after sleep deprivation and decreased by 38% after recovery, while plasma P-tau181 showed no significant changes, suggesting short-term sleep loss affects nonspecific neuronal markers.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
